subject: RE: Data transfer / SOC 2 evidence and SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Oliver Harris <oliver.harris@datatrust.eu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@datatrust.eu>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:37:00 +0000
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II + control mapping for GDPR / cross-border clarification

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. DataTrust is starting a compliance review for an upcoming pilot and we need a couple of items to complete our security assessment: 

- The latest SOC 2 Type II report (audit period and date) that covers production inference services.
- A high-level mapping that shows how Redwood controls align to GDPR articles and data transfer safeguards (particularly for UK/EU data residency and SCCs).
- Answers to a handful of SIG/CAIQ questions we flagged (we'll attach the partial questionnaire).

Two clarifying points: our procurement team needs the audit period window (start/end) and whether Redwood can provide a bridge letter to cover the period between the SOC report end and present if the audit period doesn't include the current quarter. Also confirm whether any EU-hosted dedicated regions are used for the DataTrust tenant, or if our traffic will transit non-EU regions.

Can you send the SOC2 PDF and a short control mapping doc by EOD Friday, 13 Nov? If you need a PO or DPA redline early, loop legal.

Best,
Oliver
Security Architect | DataTrust EU
attachments: SIG-vendor-questions.xlsx (sent)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Harris <oliver.harris@datatrust.eu>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + control mapping for GDPR / cross-border clarification

Hi Oliver — thanks for the note and the SIG file. We're happy to support the pilot. Quick summary of what we'll provide: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period ended 2026-09-30) — PDF attached.
2) GDPR/SOC2 control mapping spreadsheet that highlights controls relevant to data residency and access controls — attached as a working file.
3) Draft bridge letter language describing our scope and the window between the report and today; we can issue a customer-specific bridge letter that references our cloud region boundaries.

A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- The SOC 2 report scope covers Redwood's hosted inference platform (hosted API) and our control environment for the period 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30.
- For the hosted API (default), customer data may be routed through multi-region endpoints; dedicated customers can be pinned to EU regions. For a pilot, we recommend Dedicated EU capacity (we can provision a tenant in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1).

Rishi and Vanessa are on copy to help with the SIG answers and to draft the bridge letter / region confirmation. We'll turn around the partial SIG answers and a tailored bridge letter by Friday COB.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20250930.pdf, SOC2-GDPR-control-mapping.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Harris <oliver.harris@datatrust.eu>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: SOC 2 Type II + control mapping for GDPR / cross-border clarification

Oliver / team — attaching our partial SIG/CAIQ export with answers for the items you flagged. A few notes inline: 

- Data residency: For Dedicated EU customers we can guarantee that customer compute and persisted KV caches remain in the designated region. For Hosted customers, session routing may use a closest-edge model and tokens may be processed outside the EU depending on failover policy.
- SCCs & transfers: We use standard SCCs where required and can provide a DPA addendum that references SCCs and our subprocessors. If you need a custom DPA clause, let us know and we'll put LegalOps on a call.
- Bridge letter: We can issue a signed bridge letter referencing the SOC 2 audit period and confirming no material control changes since 2026-09-30 relevant to hosting and data transfers — sample language attached.

If you confirm the pilot requires Dedicated EU capacity, I'll coordinate capacity allocation and a short runbook for region pinning (eu-central-1 or eu-west-1). Otherwise we'll provide more detailed transit diagrams for hosted routes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
attachments: SIG-Partial-answers.pdf

From: Oliver Harris <oliver.harris@datatrust.eu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@datatrust.eu>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Request: SOC 2 Type II + control mapping for GDPR / cross-border clarification

Thanks — received the SOC2 PDF and the mapping. A couple follow-ups from LegalOps: 

- They want the bridge letter to explicitly state the controls we care about (encryption in transit & at rest, access control, logging/audit) and to confirm no change in subprocessors in the audit-to-present window. Can you include subprocessor attestations?
- For our procurement, please confirm the exact audit window dates in the SOC report cover page (we saw 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30) and confirm the auditor's firm name.

If you can add those details to the bridge letter and resend, we can finalize the pilot PO next week. We're leaning toward Dedicated EU capacity but need the DPA & bridge letter before comms internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Oliver
Security Architect | DataTrust EU
